title: Ensure no hardcoded credentials in webapp template
description: Audit all files in the webapp template directory to confirm no real secrets are present. All sensitive config must use process.env or template placeholders. Add a test to enforce this.
acceptanceCriteria: No JWT_SECRET values present in template files
No database passwords present in template files
No API keys present in template files
grep for common secret patterns returns no hardcoded values
A test enforces this constraint automatically

steps.description: Audit webapp template files for secrets
steps.details: Run: `grep -r -i 'password=' src/templates/webapp/` and `grep -r -i 'secret=' src/templates/webapp/` and `grep -r -i 'apikey=' src/templates/webapp/`. All results should only be placeholder text or env var references.
If any hardcoded secrets are found, replace them with process.env references or {{PLACEHOLDER}} tokens. Check config files, server entry point, and database configuration.

steps.description: Write a test that checks for secrets
steps.details: Add a Vitest test in src/templates/__tests__/security.test.ts that walks the webapp template directory and asserts no files contain patterns like /password\s*=\s*['"][^'"]+['"]/ (a literal password value).

technicalNotes: Common secret patterns to check: JWT_SECRET=<value>, password=<literal>, api_key=<literal>
.env.example values like 'your-secret-key-here' are intentionally placeholder text — do not flag these
